reviewAdvisory: The grandfathering rule, the in-transit treatment and the 'cleared on or after 30 October 2026' rule are asserted as fact but appear nowhere in the figures or the single cited Commission news article, and the FAQ later admits the article does not address in-transit cargo.

The refund entitlement is stated as a consequence of the rate change, yet the confidence section concedes the article does not describe it and it is 'inferred' - an inferred mechanism cannot be presented as a definite entitlement.

The 1.9 figure is the gap between the two low endpoints (45.6 - 39.8), but 5.8 is the gap between the two high endpoints (50 - 48.1); pairing them implies a per-producer comparison the draft elsewhere says is impossible without producer-specific rates.
€3,500 per tonne is not among the figures supplied and is presented as a market CIF value rather than a stated assumption, so every cost table and per-tonne figure rests on an unsourced number.

The confidence section labels the figures 'Confirmed' while conceding all three come from one Commission news article, and it does not disclose that the definitive regulation itself was not consulted.
The characterisation is editorial and adds nothing derivable from the figures; the percentage is already stated.
